# round-puffin — An event declares its cost in a few named tiers · filed 2026-11-01

[tiny-lark](../../playtests/2026-11-01-tiny-lark.md), #931: "yes, tiers as new item for later".

**Context.** Split from M175 (a row states what it costs, and the cost table is checked in), closed in the queue review (inbox #922). **The cost table stays as built**: `docs/COSTS.md` is generated by `tools/cost-table.sh` and checked in, so a move of any number shows in the diff where reviews notice it. The player objected to closing it for that reason ([tiny-lark](../../playtests/2026-11-01-tiny-lark.md), #927: "why close? we need this table asap so we can notice if anything changes. not sure what you mean by "checked by CI". the act of checking it in makes it show up in the diff which will  be noticed in reviews"); the table is not what closes, only the half that stops the move from happening is filed fresh here. The original words, [PLAYTEST-114](../../playtests/PLAYTEST-114.md):

> "is there a better way than having four numbers to control what actually happens? we adjust one thing but then forget to adjust other things in lockstep the balance is off."

> "we can do option 1 and take the radius into account as well. meaning we compute numbers close by and at various distances. those numbers gets automatically computed/updated but also checked in so we can see in the diff where the balance changed"

What the player feels near a source is its `intensity`, averaged over its pulse, scaled by `Baby.SLEEPING_SENSITIVITY` (0.55) when the baby sleeps, shaped by `inner_radius`, `outer_radius` and `falloff_power`, less `Tuning.EXCITEMENT_DECAY_WALKING`: several numbers nothing ties together, so moving one silently re-prices every row.

**Read as:** "later" in the player's answer is the band.
